config.text: Data and Methodology

Included Applications:

1. WUI Fire Property Awareness Viewer


Included Maps:

1. Property Awareness WUI

2. Property Awareness Imagery


Data Layers Used:

1. WUI Structure V2

2. Structure Centroids V2

3. WUI Wildlands and WUI


Data Sources Used:

Overture Buildings

The Overture Maps building’s theme describes human-made structures with roofs or interior spaces that are permanently or semi-permanently in one place. The theme includes two feature types: building and building_part. The geometry of a building is expected to be the most outer footprint—roofprint if traced from satellite or aerial imagery—of a building. Buildings have a boolean attribute has_parts that describes whether there are any associated building parts. A building_part is a single part of a building and may share the same properties as buildings. It is associated with a parent building via a building_id.

The Overture buildings dataset is a combination of several open building datasets, including contributions from OpenStreetMap, Esri Community Maps, Google Open Buildings, and Microsoft ML-derived roof prints. This dataset is available on Amazon S3 and Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, and it is distributed as GeoParquet, a column-oriented spatial data format optimized for cloud-native queries.


Sentinel-2 Land Use/Land Cover (LULC)

The Sentinel-2 Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) data is derived from ESA Sentinel-2 imagery at a 10-meter resolution. This data provides a global map of land use and land cover, produced by Impact Observatory, Microsoft, and Esri. The LULC data is generated using a deep learning AI land classification model, trained with billions of human-labeled image pixels from the National Geographic Society. The model processes over 400,000 Earth observations per year to produce LULC predictions for nine classes, including water, trees, flooded vegetation, crops, built areas, bare ground, snow/ice, clouds, and rangeland. These categories were lumped into “Wildland” and “Non-Wildland”.

The Sentinel-2 LULC data is useful for various applications, such as conservation planning, food security, and hydrologic modeling. It allows users to visualize land use and land cover anywhere on Earth and can be used in analyses that require LULC input. The data is available for download and can be used in tools like ArcGIS for further analysis.
Application Guidelines﻿

Application Description

This application allows users to view where a specific location is in relation to the Wildland Urban Interface. Once the application is open, there is a search menu in the top left corner of the application. Addresses entered here will ONLY search areas within the United States or US Territories (Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Guam, Marshall Islands, and American Samoa).

Within the Imagery map, there is a Measure option on the top left of the map. This option allows users to measure distances between items on the web map.


Find Your Property

This section provides a search bar that allows users to search locations within US states and territories. No addresses outside these locations will return results (i.e. you cannot search for Hong Kong and results appear in the search widget).

 

Understand Risks

After an area is searched in the “Find Your Property” widget, the user will be able to view the Distance to Wildland, Structure Proximity, and Structure Density. These variables combined will give property owners a relative idea of how their property will appear based on USFA recommendations on the three categories. In addition to the three categories, users are also given information on where their property falls in relation to the Wildland Urban Interface.

 

Surrounding Wildland-Urban Interface WUI Relation Map

This map provides a detailed property view in relation to the wildland. Overture structures in the map feed the information displayed in the left panel of the application.

 

Imagery Map

This map provides a visual representation of properties based on the searched address. In addition to a visual of the area, this map also has a measuring tool available to measure features in and around the map, giving the user ideas of distances to features in relation to their property.
